rows: 26. Tatungfu-Chengtu Railway. Tatung - Taiyuan - Tungkuan-Sianfu-Hanchungfu-Chengtu (See "Railways Contracted for in 1913," supra.)
Loan agreement signed July, 1913, with Franco-Belgian Syndicate. Concession to include running rights over Tungkuan-Sianfu section of Lung Hai line (No. 9).
27. Sinyang-Pukow Railway. (See "Railways Contracted for in 1913," supra.) (Terminals at Wu-I partially constructed).
Line will start from Wu-I, 20 miles north of Pukow, and run via Luchow, Liuanchow, and Kuangchow. Surveys completed.
Concession granted to the British and Chinese Corporation (1914). Line to run from Nanking via Ningkow, Hueichow, Nanchang and Pinghsiang, Branches to Wuhu, Hangchow, and Kuangtehchow.
To start from a point on the Yangtze opposite Shasi, thence via Changteh, Yuanchow, and Kueiyang to Singyifu. British concession. Length of line 655 miles, of branch. Changteh to Changsha. 105 miles.
Concession granted (1914) to La Banque Industrielle de Chine to build line from port of Yamchow, west of Pakhoi, via Nanning, Posé, Singyi to Yunnanfu, thence via Weining to Chungking.
31. Kaomi-Yihsien (Shantung province). To connect Shantung Railway at Kaomi or Kiaochao with Tientsin-Pukow Railway at Yihsien via Ichoufu.
Construction provided for under Kiaochao Agreement of 1908 (German) also by Japanese Agreements of 1918, but later surrendered to Consortium.
32. Tsinan-Shuntefu. To connect Shantung Railway with Peking-Hankow Railway.
See German Contracts of 1913 also Japanese Agreements of 1918. Later surrendered to Consortium
Reconnaissance over part of the route made in 1917.
34. Harbin-Mergen-Aigun-Blagovestchensk (410 miles). Branch line: Mergen-Tsitsihar (150 miles).
Russian concession, March 28, 1916. Loan to be floated after the European War.

36. Chinchou-Aigun.¹
Alternative Schemes.
a. Chinchou-Hailar (500 miles)
b. Chinchou-Taonanfu (320 ,, )
c. Harbin-Aigun (300 ,, )

British-American preliminary Agreement, signed Jan., 1910. Negotiations suspended owing to Russian and Japanese representations.
c. Proposal is to build a line from Durshenshan (via Hulan and Mergen.)

a. Peking-Jehol (130 miles)
b. Jehol-Chihfeng (140 ,, )
c. Chingchow-Chihfeng (190 ,, )
d. Kalgan-Dolonor (190 ,, )

39. North-Western Grand Trunk system.² Ili-Lanchow-Sianfu-Tungkuan - Honanfu-Kaifeng-Hsuchoufu-Tsingkiangpu-Haichow.
Sections.
a. Ili-Lanchow (1910 miles)
b. Lanchow-Sianfu (250 ,, )
c. Sianfu-Tungkuan (85 ,, )
d. Tungkuan-Honanfu (150 ,, )
e. Honan-Kaifeng (140 ,, )

Proposal (1909) of Ministry of Communications to connect Ili with the sea via Sianfu.
A final agreement with a Belgian syndicate for a loan of 250.000.000 francs was signed in 1920 for the construction of a line from Honan to Sianfu with extensions to Haichow and Lanchow.
Original private company surrendered its rights to the Government.
To connect with Chinese Eastern Railway.
Chinese, private. Preliminary surveys for narrow gauge.
40. Central Kiangsu Railway. Icheng-Shiherhuei - Kuachou - Yangchou-Taichoufu-Tsingkiangpu.
Surveyed 1910. To be taken over by the Government.
41. Kweilin-Chengchou (Kwangsi province). To connect with Canton-Hankow Railway at Chengchou.
Surveyed by British engineers 1909. Chinese company formed, but no funds raised.
42. Kwangsi Railway. This line would run from Canton to Wuchow, Nanning, Lungchow, and connect at Langson with the Tongking Railway system.
Sections surveyed. Preliminary survey from Wuchow to Konghow made in May, 1911.

Surveys completed. Capital to be provided, half by Chinese merchants in Shantung and half by Government. Estimated cost Tls. 10,000,000 including branch line to Lungkow. Land has been acquired earth work and culverts were constructed out of famine relief surtaxes collected on Railway revenue in 1921 Perhaps a third of this route must be re-located, however, before serviceable as a rail-bed. A motor-bus service is operated over the route at present.
Taken over by Government and incorporated in the Nanking-Hunan concession (q.v.).
Provincial gentry. Earth work and buildings at Yu Tzu completed and sleepers on ground in 1911, Taken over by Government in 1912, abandoned.

Connecting with Shansi Railway, surveys run by Ministry of Communications in 1920. Land was acquired and earthwork completed to Tsangchow out of famine relief surcharges collected on Railway revenue in 1921.
Reconnaissance by Ministry of Communications in 1919. To be built out of profits of Peking-Hankow line.
Survey by American engineers completed February, 1911.
Pose to Kutsingfu surveyed by Chinese engineer in 1911. American engineers are reported to have surveyed the Yunnan-Kutsingfu section.
52. Swatow-Sheklun. Swatow - Puning - Hueilai - Lukfung-Waichou-Sheklun, junction with Canton-Kowloon Railway.
53. Sunning Railway Extension. Sunning to Yeungkong (Makyeung River).
Connecting with Canton-Hankow Railway. To be built by Provincial syndicate.
